column2: Ever wished you could draw? Not stick figures, but a real picture you'd be proud of? Grab a pen and a sheet of paper. I'll show you how.
This is Paper Coach, and I'm Lina, your drawing teacher. I show you a picture one line at a time, and you draw it on real paper, at your own pace.
All you need is a pen, one sheet of paper, and about five minutes. The pen you already own is the right pen.
First, pick something you'd love to draw. Let's try a hot air balloon.
Every lesson shows you the picture, how long it takes, and how many steps there are.
When you start, the whole drawing comes together first, so you can see where we're going.
Then we take it one step at a time. Watch me draw a line, draw it on your paper, and tap, I drew it.
column3: Then we take it one step at a time. Watch me draw a line, draw it on your paper, and tap “I drew it.”

column2: Take as long as you like. I'll wait for you, every single step.
When the lines are done, grab some colors, and finish it in full color.
And there it is: a hot air balloon, drawn by you, in just a few minutes.
Snap a photo of your page. Bright and Scan make it shine, even in dim light.
Every drawing you make is kept in your sketchbook, so you can see how far you've come.
There are a hundred and ten lessons to draw, on eleven paths.
Plants and fruits, the sky and the weather, food and treats, things with wheels, boats, planes, space, landscapes, and a walk around town.
Every path starts simple, and levels up one new idea at a time: from a little pine tree, all the way to a twisted bonsai.
The first three lessons of every path are free. That's thirty-three drawings, like a school bus, a donut, and a little tugboat.
Ready for more? Premium unlocks all one hundred and ten lessons.
A pirate ship, a bowl of ramen, a waterfall, a monster truck, a sunflower, and a cozy little café.
Paper Coach works on iPhone and on iPad. On iPad, set it down any way you like.
Lay it on its side, and I stand right beside your paper, with the whole picture and every step in view.
Stand it up, and your drawing gets a whole sheet of paper.
Drawing with family? Everyone gets their own profile, with their own progress and their own sketchbook.
A gentle daily reminder helps you keep going. It's a small note, not a streak: skip a day, and nothing is lost.
And if you'd rather draw in quiet, turn my voice off. Every step is written on the screen too.
Before you start, a few tips. Put your phone next to your paper, where you can see every step.
Don't worry about perfect lines. Wobbly is fine, and every drawing makes the next one easier.
Paper Coach is free to download, with three free lessons on every path. So grab a pen, and let's draw together!
Every one comes together step by step, just like the balloon.
